newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Scandal may split Hungary coalition-Free Democrats.
newsitem.headline: Scandal may split Hungary coalition-Free Democrats.

text.p: A junior party in Hungary's ruling socialist-led government, the Free Democrats (SZDSZ), said on Saturday the country's widening privatisation scandal threatened to divide the coalition.
"At this moment I can only say that the coalition may break up," SZDSZ president Ivan Peto told Hungarian Radio.

Privatisation minister Tamas Suchman and the whole board of directors of the state privatisation agency APV was sacked late last week in a major scandal involving millions of dollars in irregular payments to a consultant.

The consultant, involved in negotiations about asset transfers to local munipalities, received 804 million forints ($5 million) from the agency in a case that has shocked Hungarians who have suffered a more than 10 percent slump in average real wages since 1994.
The dismissal of Suchman, a close ally of socialist Prime Minister Gyula Horn, appeared early this week to have defused tensions.
But opposition parties stepped up criticism of Gabor Kuncze, Free Democrat Minister of Home Affairs who is responsible for local municipalities, over the scandal.

Peto said key SZDSZ politicians had become uncertain over the future of the coalition and they demanded changes in the influence of the larger coalition partner, the Socialist Party (MSZP) and the SZDSZ, to prevent further scandals.
"If the situation does not change susbstantially, if we cannot find the institutional tool within the coalition to prevent cases like this, we have to face a break-up," Peto said.

The daily Nepszabadsag quoted Peter Hack, one of the most influential SZDSZ politicians as saying that the the coalition could not be saved if MSZP did not "cleanse itself" and SZDSZ did not play a greater role in decision-making.

A leading MSZP politician, who did not want to be named, told Nepszabadsag that SZDSZ wished to raise the price of taking part in the government and influence decisions on the appointment of the members of APV's new board of directors. ($1=159.16 Forint)
